english: What the warlike Cantabrian and the Scythian,
note: Cantaber: the Cantabrians of northern Spain.

english: Hirpinus Quinctius, may be planning, by the Hadria
note: Hirpine Quinti: vocative, cognomen placed before the nomen. cogitet: subjunctive of indirect question. Hadria: ablative with divisus (line 3), the Adriatic sea.

english: separated, [it] set in the way, cease
note: Hadria divisus obiecto: 'separated by the Hadria lying between'. remittas: jussive subjunctive.

english: to inquire, and do not be anxious for the needs
note: nec trepides: jussive, negative kept where it stands.

english: of a life demanding few things: flees backward
note: aevi: life, lifetime; pauca is object of poscentis.

english: smooth youth and comeliness, dry
note: levis: taken as levis 'smooth' (beardless) with long e; arida agrees with canitie (line 8).

english: driving away playful loves
note: pellente ... canitie: ablative absolute with arida (line 6).

english: greyness, and easy sleep.
note: facilem somnum is the second object of pellente.

latin: non semper idem floribus est honor
english: Not always the same for flowers is the glory
note: honor: beauty, glory (of the flowers); floribus agrees with vernis (line 10).

latin: vernis neque uno luna rubens nitet
english: of spring, nor with one, the reddening moon, shines
note: uno agrees with voltu (line 11).

english: face: why with eternal - lesser -
note: aeternis agrees with consiliis (line 12), ablative of means, felt also with minorem (comparison): 'a mind too small for eternal plans'. minorem agrees with animum.

english: plans do you weary the mind?

latin: cur non sub alta vel platano vel hac
english: Why not under either a lofty plane or this
note: alta agrees with platano; hac with pinu (line 14).

latin: pinu iacentes sic temere et rosa
english: pine lying, thus at random, and with rose
scented as to grey hair,
note: canos odorati capillos: accusative of respect with middle participle, 'having perfumed our grey hair'; possessive not in the Latin.

english: while it is allowed, and with Assyrian nard
note: Assyria: loosely 'eastern', Syrian.

english: do we drink, anointed? Euhius scatters
note: Euhius: cult name of Bacchus, from the cry euhoe.

english: devouring cares. What boy more quickly
will quench of burning Falernian
note: ardentis = ardentes, agrees with pocula (line 20); 'fiery' strong wine. Metaphor: quench = cool by mixing with water.

english: the cups with passing water?
note: praetereunte lympha: the stream flowing by.

english: Who the out-of-the-way harlot will lure from home,
note: devium: off the road, retiring, solitary. scortum: neuter noun, 'harlot'.

latin: Lyden? eburna, dic age, cum lyra
english: Lyde? With an ivory - come, tell [her] - lyre
note: Lyden: Greek accusative of Lyde. eburna agrees with lyra.

english: let her hurry, into a neat, of a Spartan woman
note: Lacaenae: 'of a Laconian woman'. comptum agrees with nodum (line 24).

english: in the manner, bound back as to her hair, knot.
note: comam religata: accusative of respect with participle; 'her' supplied. more Lacaenae: 'in Spartan fashion'.

english: You would not wish the long wars of fierce Numantia
note: Nolis: potential subjunctive. ferae: 'wild, fierce'. Numantia: Spanish town besieged by Rome.

latin: nec durum Hannibalem nec Siculum mare
english: nor hard Hannibal nor the Sicilian sea
purple with Punic blood, to the soft
note: Poeno: 'Phoenician', i.e. Carthaginian. mollibus agrees with modis (line 4).

english: measures of the cithara to be fitted,
note: aptari: present passive infinitive.

latin: nec saevos Lapithas et nimium mero
english: nor the savage Lapiths and, too much with unmixed wine,
note: nimium mero: 'excessive with neat wine', i.e. drunk.

english: Hylaeus, and tamed by a Herculean hand
note: Hylaeum: a Centaur. domitos agrees with iuvenes (line 7).

english: the young men of Tellus, from whom the danger
note: Telluris iuvenes: sons of Earth, the Giants. periculum is object of contremuit (line 8).

english: the gleaming house trembled at
note: domus is subject of contremuit.

english: of old Saturn: and you in pedestrian
note: pedestribus historiis: 'histories on foot', i.e. prose, not verse.

english: will tell in histories the battles of Caesar,
Maecenas, better, and led through the streets
note: ducta agrees with colla (line 12): the necks of captive kings led in triumph.

english: the necks of threatening kings.
Me - of the sweet mistress - the Muse, Licymnia's
note: me is object of voluit (line 14); Musa is subject. dominae: 'mistress, lady', agrees with Licymniae. Licymnia is often taken as a pseudonym (perhaps for Terentia).

english: songs, me she wished to tell, brightly
note: cantus: accusative plural. lucidum: adverbial accusative with fulgentis.

english: flashing eyes, and well in mutual
note: fulgentis = fulgentes, agrees with oculos. mutuis agrees with amoribus (line 16).

english: faithful breast, in loves;
note: fidum pectus: 'a heart faithful to loves well returned'.

latin: quam nec ferre pedem dedecuit choris
english: whom neither to carry the foot did it disgrace in the dances
note: quam: feminine singular, Licymnia; object of dedecuit. ferre pedem: to step, dance.

latin: nec certare ioco nec dare bracchia
english: nor to contend in jest nor to give arms
playing with shining maidens, on the sacred
note: ludentem agrees with quam. sacro agrees with die (line 20).

english: of Diana, crowded, day.
note: celebris: thronged, agrees with die.

latin: num tu quae tenuit dives Achaemenes
english: Surely you would not, what rich Achaemenes held,
note: num expects the answer 'no'; the negative sense is not added, 'would not' renders num. Achaemenes: ancestor of the Persian kings. quae ... tenuit: neuter plural, 'the things which'.

english: or of fertile Phrygia the Mygdonian wealth
note: Mygdonias: Greek accusative plural, 'Mygdonian', i.e. Phrygian.

english: wish to exchange for a hair of Licymnia,
note: crine: ablative singular, 'for a lock of hair'.

english: or full houses of the Arabs,
note: plenas agrees with domos.

english: when toward burning she twists kisses
note: flagrantia agrees with oscula.

english: her neck, or with easy cruelty refuses
note: possessive 'her' supplied. The object of negat is the kisses implied by quae (line 27).

english: [kisses] which, than the one asking, more she would rejoice to be snatched,
note: quae: neuter plural, the kisses. poscente: ablative of comparison, 'more than the asker'. eripi: passive infinitive, 'to be snatched [from her]'.

english: at times would be first to snatch?
note: occupet + infinitive: 'be first to', 'forestall'; subjunctive, coordinate with gaudeat.

latin: Ille et nefasto te posuit die
english: He both on an unholy day planted you,
note: nefasto die: a day of ill omen on which no public business was lawful. te: the tree.

english: whoever first [did], and with sacrilegious hand
reared [you], tree, to of descendants
note: arbos: vocative (= arbor). nepotum: of descendants, grandsons.

english: the ruin and the reproach of the district;
note: pagi: village, country district.

english: him both of his own parent I would believe
note: crediderim: potential perfect subjunctive.

english: to have broken the neck, and the inner chambers
note: penetralia: innermost parts of the house, the hearth-shrine.

english: to have sprinkled with nocturnal gore
of a guest; he Colchian poisons
note: Colcha: of Colchis, home of Medea.

english: and whatever anywhere is conceived of wrong
note: nefas: impious crime.

english: has handled, who set in my field
note: qui statuit: 'he who set'.

english: you, gloomy timber, you, falling
note: caducum: ready to fall, agrees with te (lignum).

english: on the head of the undeserving master.
note: domini: the owner, i.e. the poet.

latin: quid quisque vitet, numquam homini satis
english: What each should avoid, never for a man enough
note: vitet: deliberative subjunctive in indirect question.

latin: cautum est in horas: navita Bosporum
english: is it guarded against, from hour to hour: the sailor the Bosporus
note: cautum est: impersonal perfect passive. Bosporum is object of perhorrescit.

english: Punic dreads, and not beyond [it]
note: Poenus agrees with navita: the Carthaginian (Phoenician) sailor.

english: fears hidden fates from elsewhere,
note: caeca: blind, i.e. unseen.

english: the soldier the arrows and the swift flight
note: the verb is understood from perhorrescit/timet.

english: of the Parthian, chains the Parthian, and the Italian
note: Parthi: the Parthian shot in feigned flight.

english: oak; but unforeseen of death
note: robur: oak, strength; perhaps also the Tullianum prison (robur) at Rome.

english: the force has snatched and will snatch peoples.
note: gentis = gentes, accusative plural.

english: How nearly the realms of dusky Proserpina
and judging we saw Aeacus
note: vidimus: perfect; the near-miss is the falling tree.

english: and the seats set apart of the pious, and
note: discriptas: 'assigned, separated' (spelling discr- as in the source).

english: on Aeolian strings lamenting
note: Aeoliis: Aeolic, the dialect of Lesbos.

english: Sappho, about the girls of her people,
note: puellis de popularibus: 'about her countrywomen'; 'her' supplied.

english: and you, sounding more fully with a golden,
note: aureo agrees with plectro (line 27).

english: Alcaeus, plectrum, the hard things of a ship,
note: dura navis: the hardships of seafaring.

english: the hard ills of flight, the hard things of war.
note: fugae: flight, exile.

english: Both, things worthy of sacred silence,
note: digna: neuter plural accusative, object of dicere. utrumque: masc. acc., both poets.

english: the shades marvel at, saying; but more
note: mirantur ... dicere: 'marvel at [them] saying'.

english: battles and driven-out tyrants
dense at the shoulders, with the ear the crowd drinks in.
note: volgus is subject; pugnas and tyrannos (line 31) are objects of bibit. umeris: 'shoulder to shoulder'. Metaphor: drinks = listens eagerly.

latin: quid mirum, ubi illis carminibus stupens
english: What wonder, when at those songs, stunned,
note: illis carminibus: the songs of Sappho and Alcaeus.

english: lets down its black - the hundred-headed beast -
note: belua centiceps: Cerberus. atras agrees with auris (line 35); 'its' supplied.

english: ears, and twined in the hair
note: intorti agrees with angues (line 36).

english: of the Eumenides the snakes are refreshed?

latin: quin et Prometheus et Pelopis parens
english: Indeed even Prometheus and the parent of Pelops
note: Pelopis parens: Tantalus.

english: by the sweet sound is beguiled of his toil
note: dulci agrees with sono; laborem: accusative of respect with passive decipitur; 'his' supplied.

english: nor does Orion care the lions
note: leones is object of agitare (line 40).

english: or the timid lynxes to hunt.
note: agitare: to drive, chase.

english: Alas, fleeting, Postumus, Postumus,
note: fugaces agrees with anni (line 2).

english: the years glide away, nor will piety a delay
note: nec ... adferet: negative kept where it stands. pietas: dutiful devotion to gods and kin.

english: to wrinkles and to pressing old age
bring, and to untamed death,
note: indomitae: unconquerable.

latin: non, si trecenis quotquot eunt dies,
english: no, not if with three hundred each, as many days as go,
note: trecenis agrees with tauris (line 7): three hundred bulls for each day that passes.

english: friend, you appease the tearless
note: places: present indicative in the condition.

english: Pluto with bulls, who the thrice huge
note: ter amplum: triple-bodied Geryon.

english: Geryon and Tityos with the gloomy
note: Geryonen, Tityon: Greek accusatives. tristi agrees with unda (line 9).

english: water confines, [water] surely by all
note: unda: the Styx. omnibus: dative of agent with enaviganda (line 11).

english: whoever feed on the gift of the earth
note: vescimur: first person plural, 'we who feed'.

english: to be sailed across, whether kings
note: enaviganda: gerundive, agrees with unda.

english: or needy farmers we shall be.
note: coloni: tenant-farmers.

english: In vain from bloody Mars shall we keep clear
note: carebimus + ablative: be free from. Mars: war (metonymy).

english: and the broken waves of the hoarse Hadria,
note: fractis fluctibus: breakers.

english: in vain through autumns harmful
note: nocentem agrees with Austrum (line 16).

english: to bodies shall we fear Auster:
note: Auster: the south wind, thought unhealthy in autumn.

english: must be visited, black, with sluggish stream,
note: visendus: gerundive; ater agrees with Cocytos.

english: Cocytos wandering, and of Danaus the race
note: Danai genus: the Danaids.

english: infamous, and condemned to long
note: longi agrees with laboris (line 20).

english: Sisyphus son of Aeolus, toil.
note: Aeolides: patronymic. laboris: genitive of the penalty with damnatus.

latin: linquenda tellus et domus et placens
english: The earth must be left, and home and pleasing
note: linquenda: gerundive, 'must be left'.

latin: uxor neque harum quas colis arborum
english: wife, nor of these trees, which you tend,
note: quas: feminine plural, the trees (arborum feminine).

english: you, except the hated cypresses,
note: te is object of sequetur (line 24). Cypress: the funeral tree.

english: any will follow, short-lived master.
note: ulla with neque (line 22): 'nor any'. brevem dominum: in apposition to te.

english: A worthier heir will consume the Caecuban
note: heres is subject, Caecuba (neuter plural, the wine) object. dignior: worthier (of it).

english: guarded by a hundred keys, and with unmixed wine
note: servata agrees with Caecuba.

english: will stain the pavement, proud,
note: superbo agrees with mero (line 26).

english: better than the dinners of the pontiffs.
note: potiore agrees with mero; cenis: ablative of comparison. Pontifical banquets were proverbially rich.

english: Soon few acres for the plough the royal
note: regiae agrees with moles (line 2).

english: piles will leave; on all sides more widely
note: moles: massive buildings.

english: extended will be seen than the Lucrine
note: Lucrino lacu: ablative of comparison.

english: pools, lake, and the unwedded plane-tree
note: stagna: fishponds. caelebs: 'bachelor'; the plane-tree bears no vines, unlike the elm 'wedded' to the vine (metaphor).

english: will defeat the elms; then violet-beds and
myrtle and all the abundance of the nostrils
note: copia narium: everything that delights the sense of smell.

english: will scatter in olive-groves scent
note: olivetis agrees with fertilibus (line 8).

english: fertile, for the former master,
note: domino priori: the old owner, who grew olives.

english: then thick with branches the laurel the burning
note: fervidos agrees with ictus (line 10).

english: strokes will shut out. Not thus by Romulus'
note: ictus: the strokes of the sun. Romuli: genitive with auspiciis (line 12).

english: prescribed, and unshorn Cato's
note: praescriptum [est]: impersonal. intonsi: unshaven, old-fashioned.

english: auspices, and the rule of the ancients.
Private to them the property was small,
note: census: property rated at the census. illis: dative of possession.

english: the common great: no, by ten-foot rods
note: decempedis agrees with privatis (line 15). nulla agrees with porticus (line 16).

english: measured out, private, the shady
note: opacam agrees with arcton.

english: portico used to catch the North;
note: arcton: Greek accusative, 'the Bear', i.e. the north (cool exposure).

english: nor the chance to scorn turf
note: fortuitum agrees with caespitem.

english: did the laws allow, towns at public
note: publico agrees with sumptu (line 19).

english: expense ordering, and of the gods
the temples to adorn with new stone.
Ease he asks of the gods, on the open
note: rogat with two accusatives; subject unexpressed, the sailor. patenti agrees with Aegaeo (line 2).

english: Aegean caught, as soon as a black cloud
note: prensus: overtaken (by storm).

english: has hidden the moon, and not sure shine
note: neque: negative kept where it stands.

english: the stars for sailors,
ease Thrace, mad in war,
note: Thrace (Greek nominative) is subject of an understood rogat.

english: ease the Medes, graceful with quiver,
note: decori: nominative plural, agrees with Medi.

latin: Grosphe, non gemmis neque purpura ve-
english: Grosphus, not with gems nor purple pur-
note: Grosphe: vocative, Pompeius Grosphus. ve-/nale: the word is divided across the line end, as in the Latin; the English division follows it.

english: chasable, nor with gold.
note: venale: neuter, agrees with otium.

english: For not treasures nor the consul's
note: consularis agrees with lictor.

english: lictor moves aside the wretched tumults
note: submovet: the lictor's word for clearing the crowd; singular verb with nearer subject.

english: of the mind, and the cares around panelled
note: laqueata agrees with tecta.

english: ceilings flying.
note: volantis = volantes, agrees with curas.

english: It is lived on little well by him for whom the ancestral
note: vivitur: impersonal passive. paternum agrees with salinum (line 14).

english: on the slender table shines the salt-cellar,
note: salinum is subject of splendet.

latin: nec levis somnos timor aut cupido
english: nor light slumbers does fear or desire
note: levis agrees with somnos (accusative plural). cupido: masculine here, 'greed'.

english: base carry off.
note: sordidus agrees with cupido.

english: Why in brief life do we, strong, aim at
note: fortes: nominative, 'we bold ones'. brevi agrees with aevo. Metaphor: iaculamur 'hurl javelins at'.

english: many things? Why lands warm with another
note: calentis = calentes, agrees with terras.

english: sun do we exchange? Who, exile of his fatherland,
note: patriae: genitive with exsul; 'his' supplied.

english: himself also has fled?
note: fugit: perfect or present; taken as perfect.

english: Up the bronze-clad ships climbs morbid
note: vitiosa agrees with Cura (line 22), the subject; navis = naves, accusative plural object.

english: Care, nor the squadrons of horsemen leaves,
note: Cura: personified.

english: swifter than stags and than the driving storm-clouds
note: agente nimbos agrees with Euro (line 24).

english: swifter Eurus.
note: Euro: ablative of comparison, 'than Eurus' (the east wind).

latin: laetus in praesens animus quod ultra est
english: Glad for the present, the mind what lies beyond
note: quod ultra est: 'what is beyond'.

english: let it hate to care for, and bitter things with slow
note: oderit: perfect subjunctive with present sense, jussive. lento agrees with risu (line 27).

latin: temperet risu: nihil est ab omni
english: let it temper laughter: nothing is from every
side blessed.
Swift death carried off famous Achilles,
note: abstulit: perfect, 'took away'.

english: long old age wasted Tithonus,
note: minuit: diminished.

latin: et mihi forsan tibi quod negarit
english: and to me perhaps, what to you it has denied,
note: negarit = negaverit, perfect subjunctive; subject is hora (line 32).

english: will offer the hour.
note: porriget: hold out, offer.

english: You - herds, a hundred, and Sicilian - around
note: te circum: anastrophe, 'around you'. Siculae agrees with vaccae (line 34).

english: low cows; for you raises a neigh

latin: apta quadrigis equa, te bis Afro
english: a mare fit for four-horse chariots; you twice with African
note: te is object of vestiunt (line 37).

english: purple dyed
note: murice: the murex shellfish dye; tinctae agrees with lanae.

latin: vestiunt lanae: mihi parva rura et
english: wools clothe: to me small fields and
the slender breath of the Greek Camena
note: Camenae: Italian name for the Muse. spiritum: inspiration.

latin: Parca non mendax dedit et malignum
english: the Fate, not lying, gave, and the spiteful
note: Parca: one of the Fates. malignum agrees with volgus.

english: to scorn crowd.
note: spernere: infinitive as object of dedit, 'gave [me] to scorn the spiteful crowd'.

english: Why with your complaints do you drive the breath from me?
note: exanimas: literally 'deprive of breath', i.e. 'kill', 'distress to death'.

latin: nec dis amicum est nec mihi te prius
english: Neither to the gods is it dear nor to me that you first
note: nec ... nec: negatives kept as placed.

english: die, Maecenas, of my
note: mearum agrees with rerum (line 4).

english: great glory and pillar, affairs.
note: columen: ridgepole, pillar (metaphor: support of my fortunes).

latin: a, te meae si partem animae rapit
english: ah, if you, a part of my soul, snatches
note: te ... partem: you, part of my soul; subject is vis (line 6).

english: an untimely force, why do I delay, the other [part],
note: maturior: 'too early'. altera: feminine, the other part (pars).

english: neither dear equally nor surviving
whole? That day both
note: utramque agrees with ruinam (line 9).

english: will bring ruin. Not I a faithless
note: utramque ruinam: the ruin of both.

english: have spoken oath: we shall go, we shall go,
note: sacramentum: the soldier's oath of allegiance (metaphor).

english: whenever you go before, the last
note: supremum agrees with iter.

english: to take journey, companions prepared.
note: carpere iter: literally 'pluck the road'.

english: Me neither the breath of fiery Chimaera
note: me is object of divellet (line 15).

english: nor, if he should rise again, hundred-handed Gyas
note: Gyas: the hundred-handed giant (also Gyges); the name as in the source text.

english: will ever tear away: thus to mighty
note: divellet: singular, with nearer subject.

english: Justice and to the Fates it has been pleasing.
note: placitum [est]: impersonal.

latin: seu Libra seu me Scorpios adspicit
english: Whether Libra or Scorpios looks on me,
note: adspicit: astrological aspect.

english: fearful, the more violent part
note: formidolosus agrees with Scorpios.

english: of the natal hour, or the tyrant
note: natalis horae: of the horoscope.

english: of the Hesperian wave, Capricornus:
note: Hesperiae undae: the western sea.

english: of both of us, in an incredible manner,
note: utrumque nostrum agrees with astrum (line 22): 'the star of each of us'.

english: agrees the star; you, of Jove, from impious
note: te is object of eripuit (line 24). inpio agrees with Saturno.

english: the guardianship, shining out against Saturn,
note: tutela is subject. Saturno: ablative of separation, also felt with refulgens.

english: snatched, and of swift Fate
slowed the wings, when the people in throngs
in the theatres three times clapped a glad sound;
note: laetum agrees with sonum. crepuit sonum: 'rattled out a sound'.

english: me a trunk falling on my brain
note: cerebro: dative, 'on my head'; 'my' supplied.

english: had carried off, had not Faunus the blow
note: sustulerat: pluperfect indicative in an unreal condition, 'would have carried off'.

english: with right hand lightened, of Mercury's
note: Mercurialium agrees with virorum (line 30): poets under Mercury's protection.

english: guardian men. To render victims
and a votive shrine remember;
we a humble ewe-lamb shall strike.
note: agnam: feminine.
